sequences.title: Multihomed Segment Failure and Mass Withdrawal

intro.quote: EVPN defines a mechanism to efficiently and quickly signal, to remote NVEs, the need to update their forwarding tables upon the occurrence of a failure in connectivity to an ES (e.g., a link or a port failure).

steps.explain: The attached NVE advertises an Ethernet A-D route for the locally attached Ethernet segment.

cite.quote: This is done by having each NVE advertise an Ethernet A-D route per ES for each locally attached segment.

steps.explain: When connectivity to the segment fails, the NVE withdraws that route. Receiving NVEs update their next-hop adjacencies for the MAC addresses associated with the segment.

cite.quote: Upon a failure in connectivity to the attached segment, the NVE withdraws the corresponding Ethernet A-D route. This triggers all NVEs that receive the withdrawal to update their next-hop adjacencies for all MAC addresses associated with the ES in question.

intro.quote: Since VXLAN and NVGRE encapsulations do not include the ESI label, other means of performing the split-horizon filtering function must be devised for these encapsulations.

steps.explain: The egress NVE examines the source IP address in the tunnel header, which identifies the ingress NVE. It filters the frame on local interfaces connected to Ethernet segments shared with the ingress NVE.

cite.quote: When the NVE receives a multi-destination frame from the overlay network, it examines the source IP address in the tunnel header (which corresponds to the ingress NVE) and filters out the frame on all local interfaces connected to ESs that are shared with the ingress NVE.

intro.quote: In summary, it can be seen that Aliasing (and Backup Path) functionality should work as is for inter-AS Option B without requiring any additional functionality in ASBRs or PEs. However, the mass withdrawal functionality falls back from per-ES mode to per-EVI mode for inter-AS Option B.

steps.explain: The originating multihomed NVE sends a per-EVI route for Aliasing and a per-ES route for mass withdrawal.

cite.quote: When NVEs reside in ToR switches and operate in multihoming redundancy mode, there is a need, as described in Section 8, for the originating multihoming NVE to send Ethernet A-D per ES route(s) (used for mass withdrawal) and Ethernet A-D per EVI routes (used for Aliasing).

steps.segment: NLRI withdrawal for Ethernet A-D per EVI routes
steps.explain: After the attachment fails, the withdrawing PE sends an NLRI withdrawal for the per-EVI routes. The remote PE removes the Aliasing route and the withdrawing PE's path from its path list.

cite.quote: When the AC between the PE2 and the CE fails and PE2 sends NLRI withdrawal for Ethernet A-D per EVI routes, and these withdrawals get propagated and received by the PE3, the PE3 removes the Aliasing route and updates the path list; that is, it removes the path corresponding to the PE2.

intro.quote: In order to simplify configuration, when the option of a single VNI per EVI is used, the RT used for EVPN can be auto-derived.

fields.name: Global Administrator
fields.explain: It contains an AS number assigned by IANA.

fields.name: A
fields.explain: It indicates whether the route target was derived automatically.

cite.quote: A: A single-bit field indicating if this RT is auto-derived

fields.name: Type
fields.explain: It identifies the numbering space in which the other bytes are defined.

cite.quote: Type: A 3-bit field that identifies the space in which the other 3 bytes are defined.

fields.name: D-ID
fields.explain: It identifies the domain ID for the route target.

cite.quote: D-ID: A 4-bit field that identifies domain-id.

fields.name: Service ID
fields.explain: It carries the VNI, VSID, I-SID, or VID.

cite.quote: Service ID: This 3-octet field is set to VNI, VSID, I-SID, or VID.
